It’s taken the engine with it. A new engine from Nissan is £10,000, but we can do you a discount — £8,000.’ I laughed. My truck is worth about £6,000. Why would I spend £8,000 to fix a £6,000 truck- I told them I’d find another way.” Compare Navara Repair Quotes See the Failure Timeline 80k Failure mileage £10k Dealer quote £6k Vehicle value £4.6k Final repair 18 mo Warranty Case summary A 2012 Nissan Navara D40 with 80,000 miles and a timing chain that failed catastrophically. The owner noticed a rattling noise on cold starts. The timing chain failed, and the EGR cooler had also failed, causing additional engine damage. The dealer quoted £10,000+ for a new engine — more than the truck was worth. Model Nissan Navara D40 Year 2012 Engine YD25 2.5 dCi Mileage at failure 80,000 miles Service history Independent garage every 10,000 miles Disclaimer: This is an illustrative representative scenario based on workshop consensus and known YD25 failure patterns [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. Individual outcomes vary. Early warning The whole disaster started with a cold-start rattle. The owner noticed a rattling noise on cold starts. The timing chain failed, and the EGR cooler had also failed, causing additional engine damage. What owner thought “It’s probably fine” The truck still drove, so the rattle did not feel urgent. What it actually was Timing chain failure The YD25 timing chain stretched and failed, causing catastrophic engine damage. Why it matters Engine replacement Once the chain fails, the engine is destroyed. A replacement is the only option. If your Navara D40 YD25 rattles on cold start, get it inspected immediately. Preventative chain replacement costs £800-£1,500. Ignoring it could cost £4,000-£5,000 for a reconditioned engine — or £10,000+ at a dealer. Failure timeline From cold-start rattle to dealer shock to specialist relief. This case is a classic YD25 timing chain failure: the owner ignored the warning signs and paid the price. What the owner noticed A cold-start rattle became a failed timing chain, a £10,000 dealer quote, and a reconditioned engine from a specialist. What was happening internally The timing chain stretched and failed, the EGR cooler failed, and the engine was destroyed. “The dealer acted like £8,000 was a favour. But that was just for the engine — no fitting, no turbo, nothing. The independent specialist did the whole job for £4,600 with a new turbo. I saved over £5,000. Never again will I go to a dealer for an engine replacement.” Cold start rattle Timing chain failure Dealer quote £10,000+ engine Specialist £4,600 recon engine Workshop diagnosis The timing chain had failed, and the EGR cooler had caused additional damage. The reconditioned engine (supply and fit) is selected by default because that was the chosen route. Scope Reconditioned YD25 + fitting by independent specialist Warranty 12–24 months Lead time 5–7 days Best for Owners wanting single-point responsibility The uncertainty play The engine was not the only question. The turbo could have been contaminated by debris. The dealer presented only one path: a new Nissan engine at £8,000 (parts only). No used or reconditioned alternatives were offered. The independent specialist presented two real paths. Path A Fit only the reconditioned engine — take risk on existing turbo. £3,800 If turbo fails later: add £600–£1,200 + labour. Key takeaway: a dealer's solution is rarely the only solution. Independent specialists can fit reconditioned engines for half the price.
